topic.title: Similarity Search, Learned Hashing, and Retrieval Geometry
topic.overview: Similarity search retrieves nearby or relevant items without exhaustively comparing every candidate. This topic includes approximate nearest-neighbor algorithms, compact binary hashes, learned indexes, and multi-vector retrieval. A representative hashing method learns binary codes whose Hamming distances reconstruct distances in the original space, explicitly linking compression to the relationships that search should preserve.
topic.whyItMatters: Large collections require a balance between retrieval quality, memory, and latency. Learned representations can improve that balance, but noisy labels or mismatched similarity notions may make efficient search consistently retrieve the wrong items.
topic.evolution: The representatives extend from vector-space indexing and sparse embeddings to learned hashing and dynamic indexing. Recent work examines theoretical embedding requirements for top-k retrieval, sparse multi-vector representations, and uncertainty-aware cross-modal hashing designed to reduce the effect of unreliable labels.
openQuestions: Which geometric properties best predict retrieval failures after compression?
How should retrieval systems express uncertainty when semantic similarity and label supervision disagree?

papers.title: $\mathbbR^2k$ is Theoretically Large Enough for Embedding-based Top-$k$ Retrieval
papers.tldr: Exact top-k retrieval needs only dimension proportional to k, while robust retrieval with score margins faces additional feasibility constraints.

papers.title: No More K-means: Single-Stage Sparse Coding for Efficient Multi-Vector Retrieval
papers.tldr: SSR replaces clustering with sparse token representations and inverted indexing, improving indexing speed, retrieval latency, and benchmark retrieval quality.

papers.title: Robust Self-reflective Hashing for Cross-modal Retrieval with Noisy Label
papers.tldr: RSH combines semantic and uncertainty features so noisy or ambiguous examples have a more cautious influence on cross-modal similarity.
